utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, you can call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Ekkehard Withopf, and Ruth Karper, the case manager. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Madam Judge. Good day, Your Honour. Good day, Mr. President. On behalf of General Enver Hadzihasanovic, Mrs. Vedrana Residovic, Alexis Demirdjian, and myself, Stephane Bourgon. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the other Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is the last hearing we will be having this week, and I would like to greet everyone present. Mr. Withopf, you are on your feet. What would you like to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this is a pure practical issue. Since we today will continue with the discussion on documents, I would respectfully ask the Trial Chamber, in order to ensure a smooth running of the proceedings, to have a break of about 15 minutes once the examination of the witness is finished to allow us to rearrange our things in order to ensure that the discussion goes well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not a problem. Could the usher now bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General. Can you -- are you receiving any interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's perfect. Thanks, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So this is your last day of testimony here. Without wasting any more time, I will let the Defence counsel take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Bourgon: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I only have a few questions more for you this morning, and these questions relate to a topic which was covered by my colleague yesterday, namely that of the Mujahedin. We established yesterday, General, that I have provided three statements to the Office of the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in two of these statements - namely, the one you provided which deals with the Blaskic case and the one you provided with respect to refugees - both of these statements are silent on the issue of Mujahedin; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- well, I'll have to accept that. I haven't seen those statements. I've only seen the latest one recently, but yes, I would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your statement that you provided to the Office of the Prosecution for this specific case, do you recall stating that your knowledge of Mujahedin was limited to that found in the milinfosums produced by your battalion?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes. I already stated that I have not ever personally seen a Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the article which you wrote in 1994 concerning what you stated as being the most unusual experience of your entire military career - at least up to that point - that is, your six months in Bosnia, is also silent on the issue of Mujahedin; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you assumed operational command of the British Battalion in theatre as of 11th of May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that point in time, you did know that the brigade commander of the HVO Zenica Brigade, Zivko Totic, as well as four of his officers had been kidnapped. Did you know this?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know that at that moment there was an exchange which had been organised between the Mujahedin and the HVO to exchange foreign nationals detained by the HVO against Zivko Totic and his officers? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this exchange in fact took place on the 17th of May, which is one week after you assumed command of British Battalion. Are you aware of the holding of this exchange?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you be aware, General, that this exchange was organised solely between the HVO and the Mujahedin with the ECMM - that is, the European Community Monitoring Mission - as a mediator? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware specifically of that exchange. I was aware that the ECMM and Red Cross and others were organising a number of exchanges between HVO and ABiH at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this specific exchange of 17th of May does not bring any specific souvenir to your --

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I mentioned to you, General, that the ECMM had specifically requested the concurrence of your battalion for this exchange and that in fact the Mujahedin and the HVO officers were transported using resources from your Battalion; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it, but it doesn't surprise me because that what I call routine work in support of the ECMM.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is an event which would not have been significant enough for you to get involved as the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a lot of things for a battalion commander to do; that particular day, it was probably not a priority. I would have been entirely -- if it was going on, I suspect that I was entirely happy with it and there were no problems which needed my attention at the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And even if that event involved the full attention of all ECMM personnel and that of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That doesn't make it any more significant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you did know, General, that this exchange was solely arranged, as I've mentioned, between the HVO and the Mujahedin and that 3rd Corps was not involved to this exchange, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware that 3rd Corps wasn't involved, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this -- when you refer to the term "Mujahedin," you did mention that you've never seen a Mujahedin. And would I be right in saying that, still today, you don't really know what we mean by "Mujahedin"?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a term which is used to cover a number of people. It can be used to cover somebody who's come from an Arabic country or a Muslim country and decided he's going to assist the war, the ABiH, in Bosnia. It can be used to describe those who have, if you like, joined that crowd, who may be locals, and have put on the garb and outward appearance of Mujahedin. And it covers a number of cases from, I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. suppose, a very hard line to a very soft line on the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, it was referred at one point or in many instances that Mujahedin were in fact mercenaries, and this was the kind of information which was passed on to officers of your battalion. Are you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact -- or did your predecessor, Colonel Stewart, brief you on the issue of Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He mentioned of their presence, but we didn't get into any detail about what they were doing. He said, "You should be aware there are elements about." He didn't define exactly what they are or where they were doing -- or what they were doing or where they were based.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it that you did not feel necessary to advise your officers, your field officer, or the company commanders working for you of this fact?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were all aware of the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were all aware --

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the get-go in theatre?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From briefings both before -- after my reconnaissances -- and during. It was a subject we discussed occasionally, because there were believed to be "sightings."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what if I mentioned to you some of your officers actually encountered Mujahedin in early May and mentioned that this is the first time they had even heard of Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be surprised if they said it was the first time, but I would not be surprised that they encountered Mujahedin, because we have recorded that in some of the milinfosums.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you yourself, General, you don't know who invited or how the Mujahedin ever got to Central Bosnia, do you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have no idea of what relationship, if any, existed between the Mujahedin and the Muslim religious leaders in Bosnia, do you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, other than that they clearly -- there were people who were described as Mujahedin who therefore existed, and I assumed some coexistence between them and the local population, whether it's civil or military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't know the relationship between the religious leaders of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact you don't know the source of the financing used by the Mujahedin in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I was aware that a considerable amount of money has and I think recently been donated for the rebuilding of mosques and that sort of business from outside states.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that rumour, General, or was that fact?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- that's not facts, but it's just what I gathered from talking to people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when these Mujahedin, the different types we spoke about, you don't know where they got their supplies from in Bosnia, do you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. But it -- as you know, it was very difficult to move supplies, food, and other things in and out, which is why we were delivering the aid, in order to make sure people could survive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have no knowledge of Mujahedins, whoever they are, single or units or detachments, that these people were in fact offering money to local Muslims to join them in their endeavour to make a single Muslim state?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wouldn't surprise me, because money will talk and money makes things happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is a fact that you were not aware of.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But if you were short of money over there, which people were, and somebody is offering money for you to join them, I would suspect that would be quite a good recruiting ploy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, if I mention to you that whenever Mujahedins were mentioned, either in the milinfosums or sighted by witnesses, not from your battalion, they were reported as being either Mujahedin or locals wearing masks. Were aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that -- would you agree with me that not one single military operation was seen by anyone from your battalion where the Mujahedin were actually involved?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That doesn't surprise me, and I would entirely accept that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree with me, General, that in fact none of the milinfosums report any observations by members of your battalion of Mujahedin during any type of combat action?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in any combat action, but I believe there's one particular reference to the sighting of perhaps 80 on a date which I couldn't remember exactly. But that's certainly in one of the milinfosums.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in fact, General, one of your officers did meet some Mujahedins, or at least some foreign national citizens. And I guess you will recall a report by the liaison officers to Zenica, which is Cameron Kiggell, who did speak to some Mujahedin in Zenica. Do you recall this report?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Well over 180 milinfosums were produced, and I don't recall that particular one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can turn to the documents that you have in front of you -- do you still have those documents, or -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no documents.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please make a break between questions and answers so that the interpreters can follow you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please turn, General, to tab 11 in your binder. We did insert some tabs in your binder this morning.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the document is document number 11. It's a milinfosum, number 32. The date of the milinfosum is the 31st of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] Do you have this document, General?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the middle of the first page, under paragraph 3, it is mentioned there that the Zenica liaison officer had a meeting with some Mujahedin, and he talks about them as elements based in Zenica. And the last line of this paragraph says that "He formed the impression from their meeting that they were not under the control of 3rd Corps." Can you see this in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the same day, General, Cameron Kiggell had a meeting with Jasmin Saric. Jasmin Saric was the commander of the Zenica Municipal Defence Staff. And if I refer you to the same document at paragraph 4, you see that this is the two people who were met by Cameron Kiggell. Can you see this at paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this -- in this paragraph, if you go down and you read from this document, Jasmin Saric mentioned a few measures which were being taken by the government in Zenica to tighten up on law and order. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this would go in line with what you said yesterday that the government was still responsible for law and order in Zenica; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you turn to the next page of this document, it is also mentioned there that the conversation with Mr. Saric gave the impression to Cameron Kiggell that the Mujahedin were not under control of the 3rd Corps. Do you recall this report by Cameron Kiggell? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall the milinfosum because it talks about an Italian aid convoy being stopped. And I can recall this report now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just a quick question before we move on, General, but do you know what is a municipal defence staff?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- no, not exactly, but I mean, that's a name that could hide a number or display a number of features. I don't know exactly what it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you to turn to the previous document in your binder, which is at tab number 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a milinfosum, number 46. The date is the 14th of June. And this document comes just before the one I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] Now, General, my colleague from the Prosecution did show you this document yesterday. I would like to confirm if you look at the end of the first paragraph, which refers to a meeting you had with the commander of the 3rd Corps and his deputy commander. You recall this conversation, do you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during this conversation, you would agree that Merdan clearly claimed on this occasion that the Mujahedin were outside the effective control of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is on that same day that General Hadzihasanovic showed to you a letter written to his higher command seeking guidance to deal with what he considered to be a problem. You recall this conversation with General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this letter which he showed you, in what language was it?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see the contents of that letter?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he basically told you there is a letter.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he showed you a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It could have been a false letter.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been, I suppose, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you knew it was a right letter because you could trust General Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Hadzihasanovic, I have already said - and the Prosecution referred to it as a cunning fox - it may well have been a false letter, but at that time when somebody says that to you, I would accept it on its face value. Whether it's true or not is a different matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just -- I just would like to clarify. You just mentioned something that the Prosecution refers to it as a cunning fox. Does that come from the Prosecution, this fox business, or does that come from you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It comes from -- it came from me in reply to a question, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever discuss this fox name or nickname with General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, obviously not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you, General, to turn to a tab in your book, in the documents that are in front of you, and to binder -- to tab 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this concerns two documents that come after the ones we've just been looking at. It's a letter, the number of which is P158, and the date of the letter is the 13th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] General, can you look -- do you have this document at tab 12?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you first turn to the second page, which is the Bosnian version of this letter.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this as being the document that was shown to you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise it, to be honest. It's a document in Serbo-Croat. I cannot read Serbo-Croat. It may well have been the document that was shown me, but I can't confirm that 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I ask you kindly now to turn to the first page, which is the English version of this letter. And I'd like to go with you through this letter because I feel it is important that we get your views on the contents of the letter. Now first, would you agree with me that this letter was addressed to both the commander of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina as well as to the Chief of Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first paragraph, General, it says that "Since the beginning of the war, there has been in Zenica some volunteers from foreign countries, Arabs and Turks." You agree with this, what is said there?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see all that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's also a group of Bosnians trained by these foreign volunteers who called themselves the Guerillas. And the next line says that these groups, the Guerillas and the foreign volunteers, have not entered the ranks of the BH army in spite of being invited to do so. Can you see this from this letter?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we follow, this letter also says that "They," meaning the foreign volunteers, whoever they are, "and the Guerillas," also whoever they are, "are contemplating proposals made to them by the army Chief of Staff." Would that indicate to you, General, that as of that day something was going on between the superior headquarters of General Hadzihasanovic and these foreign elements to which General Hadzihasanovic was not a party to?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is -- well, the letter states what the letter states. Whether it was delivered or not - we will assume that it would have been, because the system works like that - and I accept what's in the letter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we move to the next line, it says that "They," the foreign elements, whoever they are, "do not want to make public their decision regarding their eventual entry into the army and they wish to communicate only with top officials of the army." Now, would that indicate to you, General, if we take the wording of this letter, that this means that as of that date they are not -- they have not entered into the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that they only want to communicate with the top levels?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That what the letter says. But you will recall yesterday I mentioned the subject of deception and the use of these Mujahedin as a deception weapon, as a genuine and quite useful method of waging war, particularly on the psychological front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, we will see a number of documents today. We will skim through a few documents, and then you can maybe give -- we can come back on the issue of deception and see if the line of measures which was taken can be referred to as "deception." But for now I'll just indicate to you: Would it be a fair reading of this letter to say that the Mujahedin want to keep their eventual entry into the army secret and that they only want to deal with the highest levels?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which is what this letter says, and I would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last line of this paragraph, would that be a fair reading of the last line, which says that they don't want to deal with the commander of the 3rd Corps because in their opinion the only duty of the commander of the 3rd Corps is to arrange a meeting? Is that -- would that be a fair reading of this letter?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the last paragraph of the letter -- sorry, the next paragraph, where it says that "These," the foreign elements, "have been in this territory even before the formation of the 3rd Corps," and that "in fighting to date they've been acting outside the usual context and even outside of lawful methods of conduct, which is detrimental to the BH state and especially to the army." Would you agree that it would be a fair reading from this paragraph that General Hadzihasanovic did not approve of what these people were doing; he knew that they were there for -- before he arrived, and that he actually disapproved and he thought that this was very bad, both for the state and for the army? Would that be a fair reading of this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be -- excuse me. That would be a fair reading. But I would also point out this is the matter that I had discussed, certainly with Dzemal Merdan and possibly with General Hadzihasanovic, in that the use of Mujahedin, whilst it might be an effective weapon, was also detrimental to their cause because of the possibility of atrocities being committed by the Mujahedin. We had discussed those two angles, that they could be a benefit but they also internationally could be a problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, I cannot show you all the documents, but if I suggest to you that this conversation where you talk about being detrimental is well after the issue of this letter.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the last line of this paragraph - and I'll finish here for this letter - says: "It is a known fact" - now, this is General Hadzihasanovic speaking - "that some state organs and high-ranking Muslim clergymen are behind them." Is by this line General Hadzihasanovic telling his superiors that there is something going on, I don't know what it is, but I want to find out? Is that -- would that be a fair reading?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I refer you to the last line of this letter, the last paragraph, the last line, where it says: "In this connection, I am requesting your stances and opinions regarding the solution to this problem because these people are in my area of responsibility and I don't want to be held accountable for the consequences of their actions"? Would that be -- is that what you would expect from a reasonable commander who has a problem, to consult his superiors and say, "What's going on?" And, "I don't want to be responsible. Tell me what to do or do something"? Is that what you would expect from a responsible corps commander?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, following this letter, General, it did happen at a later time that in one of the comments in the milinfosum the content of this letter was speculated as being rhetoric. Do you recall this event?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but that's quite possible that I would have put it in there, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would that be yourself or would that be your milinfo officer?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would combination of discussions about the Mujahedin and whether they existed or not and the letter and various other events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, would you agree with me that if you had seen the content of this letter on the 13th of June this could have helped you to understand what really was going on within the 3rd Corps and the actions taken by General Hadzihasanovic? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have encapsulated what we had discussed at the meeting about Mujahedin. I'm not sure it would have changed my opinion, and I -- well, I don't remember having received this. I don't think we received this letter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, you had during this meeting with General Hadzihasanovic an interpreter, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We must have had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not go through this letter and read it to you. It wasn't important enough for you to see the contents of the letter?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think she did, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I suggest to you, General, that further to this letter, which was written by General Hadzihasanovic, there was in fact a reply by the superior headquarters two days later and that in this reply - and I ask you to turn to tab number 13, the next one in your document -

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Judge, this -- Your Honour, this is a document dated the 16th of June, 1993, and the number is P270. It's an order from the BH army headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there seems to be a letter on the -- a mistake on the last document. It hasn't yet been admitted into evidence, so it's not true to say that it is P270. But we shall try and deal with the problem at the end of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] General, you have this document in front of you concerning an order issued by General Delic, or at least his signature block is used. I'd like you to focus on the preamble of this letter. First, you would agree by reading this letter that this is indeed a response to the letter forwarded by General Hadzihasanovic; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you focus on the preamble of this letter, which says that "Since the beginning of the war, volunteers from foreign countries and a group of Bosnians, so-called Guerillas, have been staying on the territory of Zenica." Now, this, you would agree, is the same language used by General Hadzihasanovic in his letter?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next sentence, however, is a new sentence that is added by the army headquarters, where it is mentioned "With the aim of their focus engagement in our struggle." Would you agree that this change in the preamble or the way the preamble is made is that it appears there is some kind of intent on the part of the army headquarters to do something and at least to get those foreign elements to fight alongside the Bosnian army? Would you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I turn to the order itself and paragraph 1 of the order, in this order it is mentioned "Send these groups to Igman and merge them with the independent detachment in Zuka's unit." Now, first we talk about these groups to be forwarded or to be sent to Igman, and we are talking about merging them with an army independent detachment. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you know, General, that at every level, whether we talk about a corps or at the army level, there are subordinate units - for example, the corps will have subordinate operational groups and brigades, but that the corps will also have some corps assets attached directly to the corps. You know this.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the army level it will be the same thing; army headquarters will have, in this case five different corps. Are you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the army headquarters will also have some army assets. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is -- that can be done. It's not ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this -- where we talk about here "Zuka's unit and Zuka's independent army detachment," would you agree with me that this refers to an army asset and not a corps asset?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that and I cannot agree that because I'm not aware of where the SDK independent detachment sat or its order of battle or anything. I was only aware of what was in my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I mention to you, General, that SDK actually means "Supreme Command headquarters," I'm not asking you if you know. I'm asking you if this would refer to this type of asset attached directly to army headquarters.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it means, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that what this order actually says is to kind of team up the foreign elements with this army independent detachment.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next line, of course, says that "If they refuse or in case they do not accept, it is mentioned, "Show them no hospitality and eventually disarm them." Now, I would like to focus on the word "eventually." And what would be your understanding if you received an order like this?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding was -- would be -- firstly, I'd be quite concerned. Actually, all the army commander has done is actually throw back the problem to the 3rd Corps commander and said, "You have to sort it out, " effectively. And he said, "Then start and go and presumably approach these people and ask them if they will transfer, and if they are not to transfer, then you will use further means to enable them to transfer," including, as it says "disarming."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you agree, General - I believe you said you would agree because you did mention this issue - that when a corps commander or a senior officer receives an order it is not meant to be executed blindly. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that if General Hadzihasanovic had concerns over executing the contents of this specific order, you would expect him to go back and say, "That's not okay." Was that what you would expect from a corps commander?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to turn to the next document, which is tab 14, and tab 14 is a telephone conversation between the army Chief of Staff and General Hadzihasanovic. And I refer you to the second page, line 15. At this moment in the conversation, General Hadzihasanovic appears to be mentioning or asking "regarding the information that we have received about those foreigners." Do you see this line on page 2?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then a conversation - I'm not going to go through all of it - but it appears that General Halilovic then said, "Yeah? Do you have a problem?" And he says, "Yeah, I definitely have a problem. It cannot be done that way. This is my third front line." Would you agree that what General Hadzihasanovic is referring to is that he's already got his hands full with 300 kilometres of Serb lines to maintain and an internal war in his own area with the HVO, which is his second front; and that he just cannot open a third front? Is that what this would be referring to?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it would imply. It would imply his internal front, as it were, was a problem that he didn't want to face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as we mentioned yesterday, two generals placed in the same situation might very well exercise command in a different manner but both be very effective.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And although another general today may look at the circumstances and say, "You had the possibility to execute this order," with the information that General Hadzihasanovic had at the time, then this is what we have to consider in assessing whether that assessment was right. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But having been given this order, he has to then make a decision as to where his priorities lie. And if he decides that that third front line is his highest priority or should be his highest priority, the decision will be made to deal with that highest priority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would agree with me that at that point in time we discussed the mission that was given to General Hadzihasanovic and that his mission was to maintain the front line, to create the corps, and to create the necessary conditions to fight for Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd agreed that you said that, and we also discussed that whilst maintenance of the aim was very important, I did point out that if another priority came along, then you would have to change and deal with that priority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if, General, the assessment at the time was that the resources required to take on this third front would compromise the most important mission, that it was a fair assessment at that time to say, "I cannot do it this way. I have to find another way but not to disarm them"?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one way of dealing with the problem, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, I'll go on quickly to other issues which take place later.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I just ask: It is strange with letters like this which are now produced in the court that they weren't given to me at the time. And I don't quite understand why they weren't given to me at the time, because it would have enabled me to better understand the situation. And as they weren't given to me at the time, it is odd. I'd just say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this is entirely your understanding that this should have been given to you. The only thing I can point out is that the answer to the problem was given to you by General Hadzihasanovic, a letter was shown to you, and that -- did he not tell you that he was taking measures to deal with this problem?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it would have helped his case enormously, would it not, if he had produced the documentary evidence?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That may be your assessment, General. Now, if I suggest to you that a little later on there was a further order, at least not an order but an authorisation which was issued by the army headquarters or the Supreme Command headquarters, which was an authorisation for an individual who was not attached to the 3rd Corps but who was working within the 3rd Corps to negotiate on behalf of supreme army headquarters with the foreign elements or Mujahedin. Please turn to tab 16 in your document and have a look at this authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is dated the 23rd of July, and it carries the signature block of the army commander, Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... Given to Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin. Do you know Mr. Mahmuljin?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know what position, if any, was in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you agree with me that this order was -- this authorisation, sorry, is telling Mr. Mahmuljin that he is authorised to negotiate on behalf of the commander of the army with the Mujahedin from Zenica? Is that what this letter says?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the two issues that he is to look into is, first, incorporation or the inclusion of the Mujahedin in the army, as well as the use of this unit to fight against the Chetniks. Would you agree with me that this means the fight against the Chetniks means the fight on the Serb front line?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that also what was at issue was the manner of its resubordination to the 3rd Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the last line -- the last paragraph of this authorisation gives that "The authorisation is issued with one aim, and that is solving problems on the territory of Zenica." Would you agree with me that this would refer to problems related to the Mujahedin, problems which were brought to the attention of the army commander by General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that the last line, where it is mentioned that the letter cannot be used for any other purposes, means that this was a very specific authorisation to deal with a specific problem?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it in one way countermands the previous letter, because they're no longer being taken away to the Igman organisation; they're to be left in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would that indicate to you, General, that this was indeed a more complicated problem than was initially assessed by the army commander?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It indicates to me that the army commander has now said that Mr. Mahmuljin is to come down and 3rd Corps to sort this out for themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it would give some weight to the letter of General Hadzihasanovic saying that these people only want to negotiate with the highest of authorities and not with him?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What it implies to me is that the general has gone back to Delic and said, "I can't deal with this problem. I need more assets," and Delic has come back finally and said, "Sorry, get on with it." At that stage the relationship between subordinate and commander has got to a stage where Delic has said, you know, "In question of priorities you must now deal with this."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you understand now, General, that this authorisation was for Mr. Mahmuljin to negotiate not on behalf of the 3rd Corps but to negotiate on behalf of the army headquarters.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I move on quickly, General, and if I suggest to you that further to this authorisation Mr. Mahmuljin actually forwarded back a letter or a proposal to army headquarters to incorporate this unit into -- or this unit or those foreign elements into the 3rd Corps. Now, you did not know that such a thing took place in August of 1993, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did not know either that the next day army headquarters issued an order saying that they were to be taken on board and they were to be resubordinated to the 3rd Corps by the end of August 1993. You did not know that, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that, and I assume you have the necessary documentation, but it will ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did not know either, General, that the 3rd Corps headquarters forwarded an order to the 306 Brigade saying to take them into their ranks and that this same order was cancelled and never activated. You don't know this fact -- these facts?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if I tell you that such a letter does exist and that such an order does exist and that it is dated 28 August - I would ask that you turn to tab 19, simply to look at the date - and we see that the date is 28 August. Can you see this date?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the document is dated the 28th of August, 1993, and the number is DH165, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] Do you see, General, that this letter is dated 28 August 1993?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see at the bottom of the letter that it was, in handwriting, not carried out?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would that indicate to you, General, that as of 28 August 1993 this issue was still not resolved but that they were working on it?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I turn, General, to a little later on in your tour, because I don't have -- of course, we can't go through every document. But a little later on in your tour you met with Mr. Merdan and you made reference to this conversation yesterday when you were told by Mr. Merdan that the commander of the Operational Group Bosanska Krajina or OGBK, that is, Mehmet Alagic, had been given instructions to deal with the Mujahedin problem in Travnik. Do you recall this event?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the 22nd of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 22nd of October. Now, would you agree with me that this specific -- what Mr. Merdan was referring to at that time had nothing to do with what we are talking about now of resubordination but actually dealt with five Croats which had been kidnapped by unknown Mujahedin element in Travnik? Would that recall some souvenirs for you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to refer you to a letter on the 3rd of November, when the incoming head of mission of ECMM - that is, Ambassador Garrod - and I ask you to turn to tab 20 in your document. Now, tab 20 of your document. And I refer you to page 8 -- sorry, page 7.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am -- sorry, I may have --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is a document dated the 3rd of November and it bears the number P181, the subject being a visit of the head of mission of the regional centre in Zenica -- to the regional centre in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... Conversation between General Hadzihasanovic and the commander -- and Mr. Garrod, to paragraph 10. And he was asked by Mr. Garrod -- sorry, General. I'll wait until you have the letter. It's tab 20 and page 8, paragraph 10.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have it now, 8, paragraph 10. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says in this document, General, that when asked about the Mujahedin - that is, Mr. Garrod asking General Hadzihasanovic - he said that there were several kinds of Mujahedin. There was one lot which consisted of foreigners. They were trying to solve the problem. You agree that we've seen some actions taken in this respect, would you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the solutions according to this conversation were either to send them back to their countries or to integrate them; is that what this document says?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then General Hadzihasanovic also mentions that there were also some criminals who were trying to call themselves Mujahedin. They had arrested one who turned out to be a Croat and this man dressed as a Mujahedin because it was easier to rob people. "There was no special organisation of Mujahedin. Many of them were simply criminals who were wanted by INTERPOL and it was part of the Serb and Croat plan to exaggerate their influence and he was against fundamentalism." And that he says to Mr. Garrod, "And you notice that I was drinking Sljivovica last time we met." Would you say from this conversation or the report of this conversation, General, that General Hadzihasanovic is doing with Mr. Garrod exactly what he did with you; he is highlighting the problem he has with this Mujahedin and he is saying exactly what he's trying to do and that he is indeed taking measures to deal with the problem? Would you agree that this is what this paragraph --

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That paragraph is stating that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this document, of course, is dated the 3rd of November. And you know, General, that General Hadzihasanovic was -- changed assignment as of 1 November and became the Army Chief of Staff, do you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would it be surprising to you that after this conversation -- which is close to the time that you deployed out of Bosnia or you redeployed to Germany and you were replaced by the Coldstream Guards; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to turn to the next document in your book, tab 21. And in tab 21, General, there are two documents. I would like you to refer to the second document. This document was prepared by Captain Guinness, who basically was to the Coldstream Guards what Captain Harrison was to you. I ask you to take a look at paragraph 2 and to simply read with me that it says: "The operational group in Travnik have no power over the Mujahedin and there seems to be some considerable efforts by all commanders to avoid blame. Beba Salko has had a major falling out with Alagic over it and Cuskic always refers all question up to Alagic. I think that everyone is not only embarrassed over the situation but also face is being lost, as the Mujahedin are not under control." Now, do you agree that this is an assessment that is made by the unit which came into theatre after you?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an assessment, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that this assessment is based on events - and you look at the title of this letter, "Hostages being held by Mujahedin," events which took place during the time of your unit in theatre. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we turn to the first page -- the first document in this tab. This is a letter written by the commander of the Coldstream Guards, General Williams. This letter is addressed to UNPROFOR, to Brigadier Angus Ramsay. Now, I simply ask you to take a look at paragraph 1, the last three lines, where it says: "Two missing hostages may be beyond even the power of Mehmed Alagic, commander of the 3rd Corps of the Bosnian army, as it is unclear whether he even controls the Mujahedin units." Would you agree with me that it was the assessment at that time of General Williams that the Mujahedin were not, as of 5 December, under the control of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's his assessment at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to refer you, General, to one last document, which is at tab 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a document dated the 21st of February, 1994. It is a report sent by the Security Service of the 3rd Corps to the Security Service in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] Now, this, General, is a document that deals with the Mujahedin issue. And if I look at paragraph number 1, it talks about a conversation which was held with Mr. Abu Haris, who seems to have some kind of a role with the El Mujahedin. Does that name ring a bell to you, General, Abu Haris?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does the name of the unit El Mujahed ring a bell to you, General?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this, at the -- further down into this paragraph, it talks about the majority of the foreign nationals and it talks about a conversation. And I refer specifically to line 5. It is a conversation which Abu Haris had with the commander of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now, would this letter indicate, General, that as of February of 1994 the status of Mujahedin - at least these specific Mujahedins mentioned in this letter - was still not resolved as of February of 1994?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it would indicate, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, having gone through all these documents, would you agree with me that the Mujahedin -- first of all, that we don't have the knowledge -- or you don't have the knowledge as to whether there are one, two, three, four, five, or many different Mujahedin elements? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And based on your answers to my previous questions, that you would agree that you knew nothing about the organisation of the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I've said, I -- we had a number of sightings of Mujahedin which were recorded, but nothing more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these sightings were never into a combat situation and never into an attack, because, in fact, rarely did anyone from BritBat ever notice an attack being conducted; would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that for all these reasons --

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, wrong, it would not be a fair statement. A number of attacks we did notice and were there at the time. It would be wrong to say we never noticed an attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, because you answered that you may have noticed an attack, if you had noticed an attack, it would be in the milinfosum, would it?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if the milinfosums are silent on actually sightings of an attack being conducted, this would mean that you have not seen any attacks.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would mean if they hadn't reported a particular attack, they wouldn't -- perhaps not have seen it. They may have reported it the next day as having happened, but at the time they may well not have seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I tell you, General, that all what you have in the milinfosums that deals with Mujahedin or the majority of what is mentioned about the Mujahedin is -- comes from the comment section of your milinfosum, would you agree with me that this means that as a matter of fact you never knew and the battalion never knew exactly what were the Mujahedin, what they were doing, why they were there for, and that they were not under command of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entries in the milinfosum were the best guess we had as to what was going on, and that was exactly contained as you have said in the comment. The facts when we saw them, the Mujahedin, were also included in the milinfosum. What we put in the comment was a reasonable deduction from what we had seen and had reported.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd just like to -- and I'm almost done -- in terms of -- you saw the name mentioned in one of the documents we've seen of Beba Salko. Do you know who Beba Salko is?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I've met Beba Salko -- I don't know what he is, but I've met him on a number of occasions in Travnik, where I think he was based. He had some sort of liaison function between 3rd Corps and Travnik, I believe. He facilitated movement across front lines. I think he was probably involved in some black marketeering, and he had an unusual relationship with the Serbs across the Travnik front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say that Beba Salko was a source of information that would be considered in drafting the milinfosum and your comments?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the liaison officer in Travnik or other people in Travnik received -- information they received from Beba Salko would be looked at and could be included in the milinfosum, but not always. But it was evaluated and then considered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that information coming by someone who you believed to be involved in black marketeering and to have all those -- all these special relationships cannot be reliable?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. It could be quite valuable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree with me, General, that the information in one of the specific milinfosums, if it is reported that we now have to watch for the reliability of this information because of what happened between General Alagic and Mr. Beba Salko, you would agree with me that this would not only affect your future consideration of what Beba Salko may have told you, but also what he may have told you before?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might well affect it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in such an event, would you agree with me that the information that you had from your liaison officers was always coming from people such as Beba Salko who were -- those who were willing to speak to your liaison officers?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be incorrect to say the information we had was always coming from people like Beba Salko. We got information from a number of people, from local people, from others, but not always from people like Beba Salko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. One last issue and I'm done. It's the issue of propaganda. Would you agree with me, General, that the Mujahedin issue is something that was very high on the list of priorities of the HVO, who were especially effective with propaganda on all types of their conflict with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're saying the HVO were especially effective in propaganda? Not particularly, I wouldn't have said. They used propaganda. Both sides used propaganda. It's a method to use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to you they were not effective with propaganda.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not particularly, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to refer to just one document, to give you one example. Tab 6 in your document, General. Now, this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a report drafted by the witness himself. The date of the report is June 1993, and it says "Formal complaint, HVO activities in Trnovac." That is, contained in the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... Having written this report?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I entirely recognise this report. I wrote it myself. It is based on my knowledge of that incident, and it actually reinforces my comment that the HVO's propaganda machine was poor. This was a very naive, unskilful, unsubtle attempt to discredit us, and it was actually in terms of international or even any propaganda, pathetic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, would you agree with me that this issue that is referred to in this letter refers to an event whereby the HVO stopped a convoy which was escorted by your battalion and under force did have your BritBat members on the side of the road, they took some boxes of ammunition which they then loaded onto the truck from UNHCR; took a camera -- a video camera out and filmed the issue in order to say, "Surprise surprise, we find BritBat escorting boxes of ammunition via UNHCR convoy." Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's essentially what happened, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were complaining in this document about this "pathetic", as you called it --

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- use of force against your battalion, and you warned the HVO never to use such a video on public TV because then the world would know what they're really doing. Is that what -- basically what you're saying in this letter?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I used the word "effective" a little earlier. Maybe I used the wrong word. What -- I would like to make my question more precise: Did the HVO extensively use effective or non-effective, in your view, propaganda in -- as a weapon, as a tool to get the attention and to have an impact on their conflict with the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both sides used propaganda. But I would point out that it was of -- in the HVO side, it was normally of this quality, which was poor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, I just have one last question: Do you know something about a foreign element called -- or at least an independent element called the Fishhead Gang?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe the Fishhead Gang worked -- may have been involved in an attack on some Italians on the road between Gornji Vakuf and Travnik. I have might have got that wrong, but I seem to remember they were operating in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know that the Fishhead Gang did not belong to either army and was an independent group of bandits?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it lived in an area of -- which was neither occupied by HVO or ABiH, as far as I'm aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know that they operated as a bunch of criminals and that they, for example, hijacked a vehicle of Dutch military policemen, where they stole both their vehicles and their weapons, and that they were associated with a man called Paraga?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall these --

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall the word, yes, and the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, to finish my cross-examination, I would simply like to confirm that you've had a number of dealings with General Hadzihasanovic during your stay in Bosnia and you said all kinds of good things about General Hadzihasanovic yesterday. Would you confirm that in your dealings with General Hadzihasanovic that not only did he display all the qualities that you did mention yesterday, but that always he acted in a diligent manner to any request you brought to him and that he always tried to do his best to help the UNPROFOR mission and that in your view he was a commander who was interested in doing what he was there to do and not to commit crimes?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that General Hadzihasanovic was a very capable officer, and that was recognised quite clearly on his appointment and moving across to be Chief of Staff of the Bosnian army, which is a position of great responsibility and requires a feeling and a knowledge of political events, as well as the military. And that to me was an indication of his intelligence, his character, and his ability. He was also an ex-JNA officer, I believe, of high rank, as a colonel, and therefore he knew his responsibilities as a soldier and as an individual to the way his business was conducted. He was always, as you've said, very pleasant in our meetings and very helpful in our meetings. I have not denied that. And as far as I can say, our relationships were very cordial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. One just last bit of information. I have a paper that was just passed to me. When you -- you mentioned something yesterday about a picnic. Now, would you agree with me, or maybe you did not, that this event actually took place right beside the forward command post of General Hadzihasanovic, near the Zepce area?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I -- the picnic I referred to I thought took place further south. Are you talking about a lunch in a small inn near Zepce? Because I think we had --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely, General.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one. That wasn't a picnic, that was a lunch, as it were; it was inside a building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you could recognise that this was the forward command post of General Hadzihasanovic --

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, had communications equipment there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I be allowed to make a comment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An officer called Cameron Kiggell has been referred to yesterday and today. I would just like to point out that he was a very junior officer in my organisation with limited training. He was removed from the appointment of liaison officer at Zenica and moved up to Tuzla and replaced by a much more experienced officer, who was in fact my adjutant, Captain Andrew Jackson. I'd just like to point that out for the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this concludes our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have another quarter of an hour before the break. I will now give the floor to the other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We don't have any questions for General Duncan. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to Mr. Withopf, as far as the documents are concerned, are you requesting that they be tendered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's necessary to select the documents, but I do intend to tender them into evidence. We could deal with this later, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, as far as re-examination is concerned, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I have a number of questions. It may take me some 15 to 20 minutes to conclude the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have 15 minutes before the break, so please go ahead. Re-examined by Mr. Withopf:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I have two sets of questions I would like to address with you. The first set deals with the responsibility of a commander, and the second set will address a number of issues related to the Mujahedin and all questions are asked because these issues have been addressed by my learned friends from the Hadzihasanovic Defence. Let's address the first issue first obviously. General, what effect, what effect, if any, does the fact that one side to a conflict is in a defensive posture when it comes to the responsibility of a commander to invest and to refer potential violations of the law to the legal -- to the appropriate legal authorities?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my mind, it makes no difference whether you're in a defensive posture or an attacking posture. The responsibility remains, to report violations and investigate them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What effect, if any, does the fact that one's opponent in an armed conflict may be considered an unlawful army under domestic law have on the responsibility of a commander to investigate and to refer potential violations of the law to the appropriate legal authorities?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I just delay my answer until I've read very carefully what you've just said. It doesn't matter what the nature of the conflict is at all. The laws still apply at all times. And it is one of the important things we do at the minute in the British Army, where I have a detachment of lawyers with me to make sure that when we go into a theatre everybody understands entirely the status of forces, under whose law we are bound, because we are bound from the moment we step in there, and that is very important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What effect, General, what effect, if any, does the fact that one's opponents have committed war crimes have on the responsibility of a commander to investigate and refer potential violations of the law to the appropriate legal authorities?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't matter what your opponent is doing. It doesn't change the way you do your own business. You stick by your guidelines and your laws, because otherwise your discipline breaks down and you unhinge your army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the very last question in the line of this sort of questions, General: Does it make a difference in respect to the obligation or to the duty of a commander to investigate allegations of war crimes committed by his subordinates, whether he receives the respective information from within his own chain of command, a situation addressed yesterday, or - and now I will suggest three scenarios - when the event or when the information comes from open source, such as radio and TV broadcast; if the information comes from the opposite side, more particularly the enemy; and number three, if the information comes from more the political side.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. It makes no difference. And I'm sure everybody in the court is aware of the situation in Iraq at the moment, and there have been accusations made from all those sources against the British Army. And the British Army has conducted a full investigation into those accusations, and there was a statement in the House of Parliament by the Minister for Armed Forces. That is really a graphic illustration of what has happened when accusations have been made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Let me please turn now to the second issue I wanted to briefly discuss with you, the issue of Mujahedin. In the course of the cross-examination of the Defence, you were shown a letter. It's called "Authorisation," and the letter stems from Rasim Delic, the then-Supreme Commander of the ABiH. And it's Prosecution Exhibit P202.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In order to ensure a smooth running - I don't know the exact tab in the Defence documents bundle. Can the witness please be provided with a copy of Prosecution Exhibit P202.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I understand you have in front of you the document which is called "Authorisation," of 23rd of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My learned friends from the Hadzihasanovic Defence in asking you questions in relation to this letter have suggested - and I refer to page 24, line 12 - that Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin was not attached to the 3rd Corps. If I may please draw your attention, General, to the third line of this authorisation, where it reads: "Authorising Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin, a member of the 3rd Corps Command." What would be your comment, whether the suggestion of the Defence would be right or wrong?

utterances.speaker: ALASTAIR DUNCAN [Resumed]
